subject.title: fix(config): bound state-directory .env file reads with size limit

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally treat a state-directory `.env` over 1 MiB as unusable and continue startup without applying its values?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound, but this is an intentional upgrade-visible configuration boundary: an existing oversized file changes from being parsed to being skipped.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Merge the current implementation, relying on the new warning and empty-entry fallback for an oversized state-directory `.env` file.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility contract
options.body: Pause the PR to set a different documented limit or migration/recovery behavior before changing existing state-directory `.env` loading.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the current implementation, relying on the new warning and empty-entry fallback for an oversized state-directory `.env` file.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged bounded-read work most closely matches the compatibility and operator-observability decisions in this PR.
